business_profile.business_name: Shahabad Stone Sizing, Polishing, and Tile Manufacturing Unit
business_profile.sub_category: Stone Cutting, Sizing, Polishing and Tile Manufacturing
business_profile.business_model: B2B and B2C manufacturing - procurement of rough Shahabad limestone slabs from quarries, cutting to size, polishing in two stages and sale as flooring tiles, slabs, kitchen platforms
business_profile.description: The unit proposes to polish and sell Shahabad and similar stones. Rough stones procured from quarries are cut into required sizes and polished in high polishing machine with sand/emery materials and water as lubricant for polishing. Polished stones are abundantly used in floorings, kitchen slabs, toilets in house constructions in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Slabs normally available in one inch thickness. Manufacturing uses stone cutting machine, stone polishing machine rough and smooth, lifting equipment, water pumps.

rural_suitability.reason: Raw material is locally available as major mineral in Kalaburagi district. Limestone suitable for Portland cement and Shahabad stone used for flooring are major minerals per DIC Gulbarga. Stone Polishing at Shahabad is identified as major manufacturing cluster in district industrial profile. KSSIDC industrial estate at Shahabad exists specifically for stone cutting and polishing units.

taluk_comparison.recommendation_reason: Kalaburagi taluk offers highest feasibility due to: (1) Raw material abundant - Limestone suitable for flooring major mineral per DIC Gulbarga verified, (2) Established cluster Stone Polishing at Shahabad identified as major manufacturing cluster, (3) KSSIDC Industrial Estate Shahabad 23 acres with infrastructure and railway connectivity, (4) Highest demand 829,830 population plus government tenders specifying Shahabad stone, (5) Skilled artisans available per KKRDB regional profile - polishing machine operators, quarrying skilled artisans in Kalaburagi Shahabad clusters, (6) Lowest input transport cost 5 km vs 50-70 km for other taluks, (7) Best market access via NH/SH and proximity to Hyderabad market 220 km.

seasonality.peak_period: October to May - post-monsoon and winter construction season
seasonality.low_period: June to September - monsoon, quarry extraction slows, September is month with most rainfall 187mm
seasonality.reason: Quarry operations affected by water logging in monsoon pits; construction activity slows during heavy rain; polishing operation requires water but excess rain disrupts transport via rural roads (6906 km rural roads, 4704 km kachacha roads per district profile). Summer May average high 38.5C hottest month with heatwave 44.5C recorded affects outdoor labor.
seasonality.business_impact: 10-20% production drop in monsoon due to rough stone shortage; sales remain stable as stock can be built pre-monsoon
mitigation: Stock 2 months rough stone inventory before June
Use water harvesting for polishing water in summer
seasonality.data_status: Verified - rainfall data from weather-atlas and IMD, temperature data from Asianet news report Kalaburagi reported highest max 44.5C

Water availability - polishing requires continuous water

mitigation_measures: Rainwater harvesting and storage tanks 10,000 liters
Covered workshed to protect from heat
adaptation_strategy: Diversify to dry cutting where possible
Locate unit near reliable borewell source - groundwater data shows safe category for Aland, Afzalpur, Jevargi blocks per groundwater assessment

financial_model.calculation_methodology: Monthly Revenue = Production sqm per month * Selling price per sqm (Rs 350-400 per sqm). Monthly Expenses = Raw material 55% + Wages as per EDII - 1 Skilled 12000, 3 Helpers 24000, Supervisor 15000, Manager 120000 per year per old profile adjusted + Salaries + Power 25 HP * 7 Rs * 8 hrs * 26 days + Overheads 60000 per year + Interest. Break-even = Initial Investment / Monthly Operating Profit (Expected). Based on EDII profitability where Gross Margin Rs 7.67 lakh at 60% capacity Year 1 on sales 21 lakh.

seven_day_validation_experiment.objective: Validate demand, competition, supplier cost and unit economics for Shahabad stone polishing tile unit in Kalaburagi taluk before investment

days.activity: Study competitors and local market at Shahabad cluster and Kalaburagi APMC Yard Cotton Market
days.target: Visit 5 stone polishing units including Deccan Stone Industry, Sri Bhovi unit, Kayakayogi unit; note machinery, pricing, customers
days.measurement: List of 5 competitors with price per sq ft for rough and polished, daily production, customer type

days.activity: Interview potential customers - builders, contractors, marble shops
days.target: Interview 15 builders/contractors in Kalaburagi city, Aland, Afzalpur, Jevargi
days.measurement: Number interested: >=10, price willingness 45-55 Rs/sq ft, repeat purchase intention

days.activity: Contact suppliers - quarry owners at Shahabad, Wadi, Chincholi, Chittapur
days.target: Get 3 quotations for rough Shahabad slabs yellow/blue 20-30mm, transport cost to each taluk
days.measurement: Quotations with royalty included, delivery time, credit period

days.activity: Test product/service - get sample polishing done at existing unit
days.target: Produce 20 tiles 1x1 and 1x2 with rough and mirror polish, check quality, time required
days.measurement: Polishing time per sqm, water consumption, finish quality vs market standard

days.activity: Attempt actual sales/pre-orders at APMC Yard and Shahabad market
days.target: Approach 10 retailers at Cotton Market APMC Yard and Shahabad stone dealers, try to get 5 pre-orders with advance
days.measurement: Paid orders/pre-orders >=3, advance amount, rejection rate

days.activity: Calculate unit economics with real data from Days 1-5
days.target: Calculate Revenue = Units Sold * Selling Price, Expenses = Raw + Labour + Power + Transport, Profit margin
days.measurement: Expected margin >=20%, customer acquisition cost, break-even volume per EDII BEP 46.85% capacity

days.activity: Make decision - Proceed / Modify / Do Not Proceed based on criteria
days.target: Review success criteria: >=10 customer interviews, >=3 supplier quotes, >=3 paid pre-orders, margin >=20%

success_criteria: 3+ paid pre-orders or letters of intent
Identified vacant shed or land in KSSIDC Shahabad estate
failure_criteria: Raw material cost >30 Rs/sq ft making uncompetitive vs Kota stone
Water/electricity not available at chosen site
seven_day_validation_experiment.decision_rule: Proceed if success criteria met for Kalaburagi taluk; Modify to micro sizing unit for Aland/Jevargi if Kalaburagi competition too high but local gap exists; Do Not Proceed if Afzalpur-like low demand and high transport cost confirmed

government_schemes.scheme_selection_method: Select the five most relevant currently applicable schemes based on verified business eligibility and financial relevance. Prioritized official government sources: PMEGP for micro manufacturing, CGTMSE for collateral-free, PM Vishwakarma for stone artisan skill, Karnataka Industrial Policy 2020-25 for state incentives, Stand Up India for women entrepreneur greenfield loan. All verified from KVIC, PIB, NABARD, Karnataka Industries Dept sources.

capital_and_financing.recommended_funding_pathway: Small scale: Own contribution 10% Rs 1.1 lakh (general) or 5% Rs 55k for women/SC/ST under PMEGP, apply for PMEGP loan Rs 8.4 lakh via DIC Kalaburagi with 25% rural subsidy Rs 2.37 lakh, collateral-free via CGTMSE guarantee. Medium scale Rs 20.25 lakh EDII model: Own contribution 25% Rs 5.06 lakh as per EDII means of finance promoter contribution 5.06 lakh and bank finance 15.19 lakh at 75% of fixed assets. Can also apply Stand Up India if woman entrepreneur for loan Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore composite. State level: Apply for KSSIDC Shahabad industrial estate shed/plot allotment - 1 vacant shed available, and CEDOK EDP training for interest subsidy startup loan. PM Vishwakarma if traditional stone artisan family for toolkit Rs 15000 and concessional loan Rs 1-2 lakh at 5%.
capital_and_financing.important_distinction: Business investment and government-scheme own contribution are different concepts. Business investment total project cost Rs 9.5 lakh small, Rs 20.25 lakh medium includes land, building, machinery, working capital. Own contribution is promoter equity - 10% general (Rs 95k small) or 5% special under PMEGP, 25% under EDII model Rs 5.06 lakh. Loan requirement is balance after own contribution and subsidy. Subsidy/support is margin money 15-35% under PMEGP kept as deposit.

final_feasibility.strongest_reason_to_consider: Kalaburagi taluk has highest feasibility 84/100 because raw material is locally abundant as major mineral and Shahabad stones per DIC and NABARD district profile, established stone polishing cluster at Shahabad with KSSIDC industrial estate 23 acres 1 vacant shed, skilled artisans available, highest demand 829,830 population plus government tenders specifying Shahabad stone, and best market access via Shahabad railway station and Hyderabad market 220 km.
final_feasibility.biggest_risk: High competition in Shahabad cluster and royalty hike from Rs 70 to Rs 80 per tonne increasing input cost plus water scarcity in dry climate 5-45C with decreasing rainfall trend
final_feasibility.minimum_viable_startup: Small scale micro unit Rs 9.5 lakh with own land, single polishing machine, 500 sqm per month capacity, workshed in KSSIDC Shahabad estate or rented shed to reduce building cost, targeting local builders and APMC Yard retailers
final_feasibility.recommended_scale_for_beginner: Small scale Rs 9.5 lakh to start with PMEGP support 25% rural subsidy, then scale to medium Rs 20.25 lakh EDII model after 1 year when customer base established and break-even reached at 46.85% capacity
final_feasibility.recommended_validation_before_investment: Conduct 7-day market validation experiment as detailed - visit 5 competitors at Shahabad, interview 15 builders, get 3 quarry quotations, test polish 20 tiles, attempt 3 pre-orders at APMC Yard Cotton Market, calculate unit economics
final_feasibility.loan_readiness: Ready for PMEGP with 10% own contribution and EDP training certificate from CEDOK; CGTMSE collateral-free guarantee available up to Rs 2 crore; Stand Up India ready for women entrepreneurs with greenfield project
final_feasibility.overall_data_confidence: Medium - Verified data for geology, cluster, industrial estate, population, climate, government schemes from official sources; Estimated data for investment, revenue, expenses based on EDII 2015 project profile adjusted for current prices; Not Verified for exact competitor counts in Aland/Afzalpur/Jevargi due to lack of taluk-level Udyam database
